tweets.text:
this is all you need to build a million dollar startup in 2026

here's the actual stack (and how to make a profitable startup in a weekend):

1\ code editor
> cursor (this is your entire engineering team now)

2\ market research
> perplexity for deep dives
> gemini for data analysis

3\ writing assistant
> chatgpt, claude, or grok
> pick one, master it, stop switching

4\ design tools
> midjourney for concepts
> recraft for brand assets
> figma for ui/ux
> canva for quick social content

5\ operations layer
> reccloud for video translation
> tidio for customer service
> zapier to connect everything
> calendly for calls
> picwish for image editing

here's how this actually works:

step 1: find a real problem
> use perplexity to research complaints online from twitter, linkedin, and reddit posts
> use gemini to analyze patterns in what people hate
> validate the problem you're solving before you build anything

step 2: build fast
> cursor + claude can ship an mvp in a weekend
> stop perfecting, once that one main feature works, launch it

step 3: design that converts
> midjourney for hero images that stop the scroll
> canva for consistent social presence
> figma only when you're ready to scale

step 4: automate everything
> zapier connects your tools so you sleep
> tidio handles support while you build
> calendly books calls without the back and forth

step 5: distribution (the part everyone skips)
> write content with ai assistance
> but make it sound like you
> share real numbers, real failures, your experience building, lows and highs etc

the tools don't build the startup. the person using the tools do

tweets.text:
Building the right team is the hardest part of an early-stage startup.

When the team is small, every decision matters more and every hire changes the dynamic of the room.

How the team gets work done is set by the people in the room. That's why we've been intentional about the values we build around.

Here’s how we think about it at @boardyai:

1. Have fun.
It’s hard to fake laughter. When people are laughing, you’re usually getting the honest version of them. When work gets intense, it’s easy to forget that this is the first value. @goswish and @owengretzinger tell a joke during standup every morning, and it’s a simple reminder that work should still feel fun.

2. Pick up the phone.
People often call Boardy at inflection points, like when a term sheet comes in, a negotiation gets tricky, or they’re unsure what to do next. Being there for each other matters. A lot of people on the team have gotten cold calls from me, and they’ll probably get more.

3. Use your imagination.
Boardy started as an idea. There’s rarely one right way to do something. When you think about what’s possible with the tools we have now, you see more ways to approach a problem. We stay open to new approaches and give the team room to try them.

4. Gas up the jet.
We want to win. We’re building something ambitious and unusual, and we take that responsibility seriously.

This is the attitude we want to hold onto as we grow, and we don’t take lightly the people who choose to do this work with us.
